keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Insubres row and the page has no infobox area. 'Their frontier with the Cenomani probably ran along the Oglio in the 3rd century BC', so the Lombardy region is cut at the Cenomani provinces. Soft edges. From 222 to November 218 Rome holds the land (loss 222, gain 218): no keyframe for those years.

keyframe_review.note: Same shape as -396..-223; the Insubres 'went over to Hannibal' in 218 and fight the reconquest until 197 (a contest with Rome, 'from 201 BC' the Roman reconquest).

correction.text: 'The Insubres held the western part of the Transpadane plain, in central Lombardy'; 'their land lay between the Ticino and the Oglio', chief town Mediolanum; Lombardy without Brescia, Cremona and Mantova (east of the Oglio, the Cenomani's); bound to Rome by a treaty (foedus)

keyframe_review.note: Same shape; from 197 the Insubres are a treaty ally of Rome, so the renderer tints the land as a client (vassal_start 197, vassal_end 89, matching roman-republic /ledger/80 and /138). The Latin rights of 89 end the people's separate existence.

ledger.note: c. 396 BC: the Insubres 'held central Lombardy, with Mediolanum (modern Milan) as their chief town', 'between the Ticino and the Oglio' (Insubres page: land from 'the trans-Alpine invasion of the 4th century BC', no year); the Etruscan civilization page gives 'from 396 BC: Invasion of the Celts into the Po Valley', which the etruscans dossier (/ledger/14) turns into a loss of Lombardy to the Insubres, so the year follows it. Brescia, Cremona and Mantova, east of the Oglio, are the Cenomani's (cenomani dossier).
225-222 BC: Telamon (225), the Oglio (223), Clastidium and Mediolanum (222).
222 BC: 'After Acerrae and then Mediolanum fell, the Insubres were forced to surrender' (the roman-republic dossier colours Insubria Roman 222-218).

218 BC: 'The Insubres went over to Hannibal after he crossed the Alps that year'; the Boii and Insubres 'besieged Mutina' (Cisalpine Gaul page). The roman-republic dossier's loss of the Po valley (218, month 11) names 'boii'; Insubria returns here.
218-197 BC: the Hannibalic war and the Roman reconquest 'from 201 BC'.
197 BC: 'The Insubres submitted in 197 BC, and the coalition was broken after two battles near Mediolanum in 194 BC'.

197 BC: 'The Insubres submitted in 197 BC'; Rome 'bound the Insubres, like the Cenomani, by a treaty' (foedus), so the land stays Insubrian but is tinted from roman-republic (vassal_start insubres 197).
89 BC: 'The lex Pompeia of 89 BC granted Latin rights to the Transpadani', ending the foedus (roman-republic vassal_end insubres, month 12).
89 BC: Latin rights; 'full Roman citizenship followed in 49 BC', 'in which the Insubres ceased to exist as a distinct people'.

wars.name: Insubrian war of 223-222 BC
wars.outcome: Roman victory on the Oglio (223), Clastidium and the fall of Mediolanum (222)

certainty.note: Central Lombardy between the Ticino and the Oglio; the Oglio frontier with the Cenomani is 'probable' (page); the region is the roman-republic dossier's Lombardy cut at the Cenomani provinces.

notes: New state. Insubria from a 400 placeholder to the submission of 197 (then tinted from roman-republic to 89). The Roman conquest of 222 and the rising of 218 are mirrored as loss and gain, so the state has no land for 222-218 (month 11) while Rome colours it; a compiler that cannot show a landless state may prefer to treat 222-218 as a Roman occupation. Wikidata unverified. Revised 2026-10-19 after review: the dossier now runs to 89 (month 12) with the foedus as vassal_start 197 and vassal_end 89, as roman-republic /ledger/80 and /138 have it (so eu-03-b need not drop the tie); every Lombardy region is Lombardy minus Brescia, Cremona and Mantova (the Insubres page: land between the Ticino and the Oglio, frontier with the Cenomani on the Oglio); the founding moves from the placeholder 400 to 396 with counterpart etruscans, to agree with etruscans /ledger/14 (the Etruscan civilization page, reopened, dates the Celtic invasion of the Po valley 'from 396 BC'; the Insubres page gives only 'the 4th century BC'); keyframes added.
